title.value: Fast and Slow Learning of Recurrent Independent Mechanisms
title.justification: The title provides a comprehensive understanding of the focal points of the research, namely the methodological approach (fast and slow learning) and the primary concept being investigated (Recurrent Independent Mechanisms).
title.quote: F AST AND S LOW L EARNING OF R ECURRENT I NDEPEN- DENT M ECHANISMS

analysis.description: The paper investigates the use of meta-learning combined with modular architectures in reinforcement learning setups to adapt to changes in distribution and tasks rapidly. It proposes an architecture based on Recurrent Independent Mechanisms (RIMs) which use dynamic attention to allow specific modules to update rapidly while maintaining others over longer time spans. This method aims to address the issue of systematic generalization and adaptation to novel situations.

type.justification: The paper conducts experiments using modular architectures in reinforcement learning environments, providing empirical evidence through experiments to demonstrate the efficacy of their proposed method.
type.quote: We evaluate the proposed Meta-RIMs networks to answer the following questions: (a) Does the proposed method improve sample efficiency? We answer this positively in section 4.1.

name.justification: The paper discusses a reinforcement learning setup involving navigation in partially observed environments as the main experimental setup.
name.quote: We find that meta-learning the modular aspects of the proposed system greatly helps in achieving faster adaptation in a reinforcement learning setup involving navigation in a partially observed grid world with image-level input.

name.justification: The use of meta-learning techniques is central to the paper's proposed approach for updating model parameters differently over time.
name.quote: Meta-learning is directed towards sample efficiency in the face of changes in distribution and tasks.
